writer.markdown:
## Company overview

JPMorgan Chase & Co. is a bank and financial holding company operating in the United States, the rest of North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, the Asia Pacific, Latin America and the Caribbean. It reports three segments: Consumer & Community Banking, Commercial & Investment Bank, and Asset & Wealth Management. Its products include deposits, investment and lending products, cash management, mortgage origination and servicing, credit cards, payment solutions and auto loans. With a market capitalisation of $883.53B, it sits in the Banks - Diversified industry within Financial Services.

## Financial commentary

Revenue grew every year in the period shown, from $127.73B in fiscal 2022 to $154.95B in 2023, $169.44B in 2024 and $181.85B in 2025. Net income rose from $37.68B in 2022 to $49.55B in 2023 and peaked at $58.47B in 2024, before easing to $57.05B in 2025, so earnings did not keep pace with revenue in the latest year. The net margin is 34.9%, return on equity is 17.8%, and reported revenue growth is 30.4%. The shares trade at 332.38, within a 52-week range of 279.10 to 366.50, and the dividend yield is 2.0%.

## Comps commentary

The primary multiple for this peer set is price-to-book. JPMorgan's P/B of 2.5 is 65% above the peer median of 1.5, with only Morgan Stanley higher among the peers at 2.8, while Goldman Sachs matches it at 2.5. Its forward P/E of 13.3 is 30% above the median of 10.2, whereas its trailing P/E of 14.2 is just 3% above the median of 13.8, so the premium is concentrated in forward and book-value measures. The premium coincides with stronger fundamentals: ROE of 17.8% is 41% above the median of 12.6%, and revenue growth of 30.4% is 81% above the median of 16.8%. The dividend yield of 2.0% is 16% below the median of 2.4%. Analysts' mean target is 375.81, with a consensus recommendation of buy, though this is third-party opinion and not our signal.

## Risk commentary

The three most severe risks, each rated 3, are regulatory, legal and macroeconomic. The businesses are highly regulated and heavily shaped by law and supervisory expectations. The firm also faces significant exposure to civil and governmental proceedings, including litigation, investigations and enforcement actions. Adverse economic and market conditions could hurt results and investment and market-making positions.

Rated 2 are interest rate and credit spread shifts, which could affect earnings, liquidity and capital; deterioration in the financial condition of clients, counterparties and central counterparties; and exposure of the consumer businesses to economic weakness and governmental policy. The recent headlines concern institutional shareholding, analyst price targets and a share price move, and none relates directly to these risks.
